pageCache.pageTitle: English | Trinity St Stephen Church of England (Voluntary Aided) First School
pageCache.text:
English
At Trinity St Stephen we believe that giving children the skills they need to read and access text is a priority. We want our children to be confident in being able to read different kinds of text and to use them for a variety of reasons.
The foundation to good reading is being able to decode text. Simply put, this is being able to make sense of letters and words. To give our children the best chance of being able to do this as soon as they are able we use Monster Phonics. You can find out more about the Synthetic phonics approach at this website http://www.getreadingright.co.uk/synthetic-phonics/
You can also find videos of the phonic sounds here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-ksblMiliA8
We believe that children should learn skills of understanding and comprehending text alongside learning basic phonics skills. So through guided reading children get the opportunity to read texts together and to talk about them. They are directed to make links with the phonics they are using to read, with the phonics they are using to spell words in their writing.
Each week your child will bring home reading books relevant to their current reading level and the reading skills/strategies we are teaching them. The reading books will either be a selection of instructional level books ( where children are using a new strategy/skill to add to the range they have) and confidence building books within that level ( that ensure children have successfully added their previous new skill/strategy to their reading). We use books from a range of reading schemes ( Oxford Reading Tree, Rigby Star, PM readers) together with ‘real books’ or non-scheme books for example Usborne Young readers to paperbacks incorporating children classics and popular authors such as Michael Morpurgo, Francesca Simon, and Cressida Cowell.
We ask you to spend time reading these books together and talking about them with each other. Please tell us and your child how they are doing by using the reading record book. Whenever you get the opportunity, it is good to introduce your children to different kinds of books, for example: non-fiction books of different types; short-stories; longer stories; child-friendly magazines and newspapers - so that they begin to get the idea that they will need to use their reading skills in a variety of ways.
Praise your child for all the strategies they are using and how well they are progressing. It is also useful for teachers to know:

pageCache.pageTitle: A Peek of the Week in Year 4: A great start to the new year.  | Trinity St Stephen Church of England (Voluntary Aided) First School
pageCache.text:
A Peek of the Week in Year 4: A great start to the new year.
The children have settled back into the new term wonderfully and have made an enthusiastic start to their learning.
In Science, we have begun our exciting new topic on digestion. The children explored the digestive system using a model to help them understand the function of each organ and how food is processed by the body. They were fascinated to discover the journey food takes through the digestive system.
In Geography, our topic this term is "The UK: Who Are We?" The children have been learning about the countries and regions that make up the United Kingdom. They have developed their understanding that the countries of the UK are divided into smaller areas known as regions and counties.
In Maths, we have been focusing on place value. The children particularly enjoyed creating number lines and using their knowledge to identify and calculate missing numbers.
During Guided Reading, some of the children have started reading The Butterfly Lion. They have thoroughly enjoyed the first chapter and are already eager to find out what happens next.
In English, we have been exploring The Whale and the children have thoroughly enjoyed studying the beautiful illustrations throughout the book. As the story is told entirely through pictures, the children have been developing their inference and comprehension skills by carefully examining the images and discussing what they think is happening. They have also answered a range of questions about the story, using visual clues to support their ideas and interpretations.
We are very proud of how well the children have settled back into school and look forward to another fantastic term of learning.

pageCache.text:
Before and After School Care
At Trinity St Stephen First School we aim to support working parents in the best possible way. We now offer care for children from 8am in the morning until 6pm in the evening from Monday to Thursday. Both before and after school care is run on the school site and led by members of our staff. Details are:-
Breakfast Club – led by Mrs Rogan and Ms Ternyak
Drop off is from 8am via the main entrance. The cost is £3.50 per session, either booked in advance online via Scopay or, space permitting, turn up on the day.
Please note that on a Thursday morning Mr Brooker also runs Active Club. This is a club which encourages children to get active and play games outside (weather permitting) If spaces allow children who are booked onto Breakfast Club are able to choose this club if they wish.
After School Club – led by Mrs Kate Rogan and assisted by Ms Ternyak and Mr Brooker.
There are two sessions which can be booked online for Monday through to Thursday:-
3.15pm to 5.pm - £15 per session
3.15pm to 6pm - £18 per session
If you would like to find out more information please contact the school office: office@tssfirst.co.uk

pageCache.text:
Zoolab Visits Reception Class 2026
An animal handler from Zoolab visited reception class. He came with a selection of animals including a giant African snail, a giant millipede, cockroaches, a treefrog and a large gecko. We learnt a lot about each animal and we could also handle them all, except the tree frog, if we wanted to. It was great fun and we learnt so much!
